nodes.label: desktop memory - heed user intent, do not correct it

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. MY WORDS ARE THE CANON - the user's literal framing. When he defines how his thing works, even phrased as a question, that definition IS the specification: build to it, do not treat his input as confusion or a misconception to refute, and do not assume the agent's own context, web references or textbook norms outrank his stated intent. Trigger case 1: he asked whether the NIM calls were async with a concurrency and 40-RPM cap, and a stale v2-era memory was used to lecture him that there was no concurrency and nothing to fix. Trigger case 2, the eval cutoff k, with two compounding failures over many turns: overriding his design with a production-RAG and answer-quality-tuning frame, and worse, collapsing a distinction he explicitly drew between TWO numbers - k as the global ceiling, fixed and shared across arms and set for feasibility, and top-k as each arm's actual return under that ceiling, per-arm, the thing measured, where the token-cost gap IS the experiment - which deleted the measurement itself. The tell: if about to write 'but the references say', 'production does X', 'the optimal is Y' or 'that presupposes Z' against a design he already defined, stop, because that is drift.
